messages.author: 5ccb721d28384a05
messages.subject: PDtoMSstatsPTMFormat
parts:
Hello,

I'm trying to run MSstatsPTM on some ubiquitin enriched data from proteome discoverer using TMT quantification.

When I try to run PDtoMSstatsPTMFormat, I get this error 

Error in `[.data.table`(pd_input, , pd_cols, with = FALSE) : column(s) not found: PrecursorArea

As it is TMT labelled data there is not a column for 'Precursor Area' in my PTM input data, but I noticed there is no way to specify TMT labelling in the PD format (I could see this as an option for MaxQuant --> labeling_type = "TMT"). 

Therefore, I wondered if it was possible to use MSstatsPTM for TMT labelled PTM data from PD?

Any help would be much appreciated :)

Sam

messages.author: 3f7dab23a7bc0436

Thanks,

messages.author: 13904eb0f06097b0
messages.subject: Re: PDtoMSstatsPTMFormat
parts:
Hi Sam,

We have implemented a fix for this problem.

First, we believe you are on an older version of R (pre-4.3). Can you check if this is the case, and upgrade to 4.3 if it is indeed older? Bioconductor will not install the newest versions of packages if your R is not up to date. We believe this will fix the missing parameter options you noted (e.g., labeling_type). 

Second, from your dataset, we did notice that the original converter was setup to only work with the "Sequence" column, not the "Annotated Sequence" column. Given the non-PTM PD TMT datasets we have, we have decided to switch the converter to work with the "Annotated Sequence" column. To do this we needed to push a bug fix to Bioconductor. This bug fix will be reflected on the platform tomorrow around noon eastern time. You can either wait until Bioconductor is updated tomorrow, or install the package directly from Github now. 

I have provided code below to both install the package from Github and run the converter. Note the newest version of the converter requires a FASTA file. I have included one for the dataset you provided to this message, but you may want to pull your own. 

Let me know if you have any questions!

Devon


```
devtools::install_github("https://github.com/Vitek-Lab/MSstatsPTM")

library(MSstatsPTM)

pd_input = read.csv("PD_input_subset.csv")
annotation = read.csv("PD_annotation.csv")

msstats_input = PDtoMSstatsPTMFormat(
  pd_input,
  annotation=annotation,
  fasta_path="idmapping_2024_01_16.fasta",
  mod_id="\\(GG\\)",
  labeling_type = "TMT",
  use_localization_cutoff=FALSE,
  which_proteinid = "Master.Protein.Accessions")
```

Hi Sam,

We have implemented a fix for this problem.

First, we believe you are on an older version of R (pre-4.3). Can you check if this is the case, and upgrade to 4.3 if it is indeed older? Bioconductor will not install the newest versions of packages if your R is not up to date. We believe this will fix the missing parameter options you noted (e.g., labeling_type). 

Second, from your dataset, we did notice that the original converter was setup to only work with the "Sequence" column, not the "Annotated Sequence" column. Given the non-PTM PD TMT datasets we have, we have decided to switch the converter to work with the "Annotated Sequence" column. To do this we needed to push a bug fix to Bioconductor. This bug fix will be reflected on the platform tomorrow around noon eastern time. You can either wait until Bioconductor is updated tomorrow, or install the package directly from Github now. 

I have provided code below to both install the package from Github and run the converter. Note the newest version of the converter requires a FASTA file. I have included one for the dataset you provided to this message, but you may want to pull your own. 

Let me know if you have any questions!

Devon


```
devtools::install_github("https://github.com/Vitek-Lab/MSstatsPTM")

library(MSstatsPTM)

pd_input = read.csv("PD_input_subset.csv")
annotation = read.csv("PD_annotation.csv")

msstats_input = PDtoMSstatsPTMFormat(
  pd_input,
  annotation=annotation,
  fasta_path="idmapping_2024_01_16.fasta",
  mod_id="\\(GG\\)",
  labeling_type = "TMT",
  use_localization_cutoff=FALSE,
  which_proteinid = "Master.Protein.Accessions")
```
